original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

scope_change_reason: Open PR #3731 measured the length-22 resource budget with the corrected engine and named two next steps: a higher probe level or a cheaper proved prune, and specifically asked whether the pair identity in #2973's MATH.md section 3 can become a third monotone prune. It cannot: the identity gives a leaf LOWER bound on a monotone increasing partial quantity, which is the wrong direction for branch rejection. The merged independent census #3005 proves a different, genuinely stronger completion bound on the union of the same-parity pair supports. This package ports exactly that bound into the fast corrected engine, proves it dominates the even excess budget, and re-runs the L22 splits. The active decision it can change is how much of the L22 split domain is excluded at a defensible cost; no larger search or new mechanism is claimed.
actual_scope: One new necessary bound in the corrected seven-label census engine: |supp EE union supp OO| + C(S,2)+C(T,2)-C(e,2)-C(o,2) >= 2^(n-1)-1, enabled by default with --no-union-budget as the predecessor mode. Validation against the predecessor's raw-product brute force on all small splits and all budget modes, a union-only mode, and the six recorded L20/L18 zero-hit receipts (result, not node count). Length-22 probes use the same fifteen restricted-growth prefix shards for every split; completed zero-hit runs are finite split exclusions, capped runs are tree-size lower bounds only.
bottleneck_link: The census-pruning-audit card asks which pruning implications are sound before an exclusion is relied on. The L22 word census is the live downstream consumer of #2973's corrected engine; a strictly stronger, proved bound cuts its cost without weakening any stated scope, and a completed split is a new finite exclusion inside PR943's prefix-walk model.
stop_rule: Stop after the six open L22 splits have been run under the shard cap or the session budget is exhausted. A split with any capped or failed shard is recorded as a lower bound only and never as an exclusion. Any hit word is reported verbatim and the exclusion claim is withdrawn.
evidence: RESULT.json: pinned predecessor hash and committed engine DELTA.diff, predecessor math check exit 0, brute-force cross-check exit 0 over all small splits and budget modes, union-only small-domain check, six L20/L18 zero-hit receipt replays, and sharded L22 probes for the six open splits with per-shard caps. See README.md for the exact completed/aborted split list and node counts.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a restored universal length-22 seven-label word exist (f(7) = 22 versus 24)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: #2973 bounds 22 <= f(7) <= 24; a complete zero-hit nine-split census would give f(7) = 24 inside PR943's prefix-walk model.
open_questions.first_step: Re-run any split this package leaves capped with a larger per-shard cap, or add a further proved completion bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: The remaining splits' measured lower bounds exceed one session's shard budget; see RESULT.json.

open_questions.question: Can the exact pair identity sum_y C(r_y,2) = 2 sum_x A_x B_x yield a monotone branch prune?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #3731 named it as the cheapest possible third prune.
open_questions.first_step: Note that sum_x A_x B_x is monotone increasing in the state while the leaf identity supplies a LOWER bound, so the direct inequality cannot reject a partial state. A usable prune needs a leaf upper bound, which is what the union support bound supplies.
open_questions.blocked_by: No monotone upper-bound variant of the identity is known; the raw identity is the wrong direction.
